_comment: Curated, version-controlled CVE disposition overlay for the distro-backport pipeline. Highest precedence: merged into cve.db's backports table LAST (INSERT OR REPLACE), so these analyst-verified entries override the auto-sourced OSV (AlmaLinux/Debian/Ubuntu) and Red Hat securitydata data. This is the 'improve over time' store — add an entry whenever triage (e.g. a credentialed `rpm -q --changelog` check, or an accepted-risk decision) establishes a disposition the auto feeds don't carry. Reviewed on every CVE DB rebuild. Each entry is scoped per (cve, distro, release, package); use distro 'AlmaLinux' as the el8/el9 family proxy (RHEL/CloudLinux/Rocky/CentOS). disposition is one of: fixed (suppressed; set fixed_version), not_affected (suppressed), false_positive (suppressed; stored as not_affected), wont_fix (active + badged), fix_deferred (active + badged), affected (active). For product-scoped (non-distro) false positives, use checkfix_test/resources/cve_false_positives.json instead.

_example.reason: Confirmed via rpm -q --changelog: vulnerable code path not compiled in el8.

dispositions.reason: No el8 backport (Red Hat Will-not-fix). Not remotely exploitable: the authentication bypass requires a local Rowhammer/DRAM bit-flip primitive (CVSS AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) - an unprivileged attacker already executing code on the same physical host, with Rowhammer-susceptible (non-ECC/unmitigated) DRAM, landing a precise single-bit flip on the 'authenticated' integer in mm_answer_authpassword. Unreachable by an external unauthenticated scan; software fixes are ineffective by design (hardware fault, disputed upstream). Banner-version match only; CVSS 7.0 overstates remote risk. Downgraded for external/PCI context per accepted-risk triage.

OPIE/PAM is not part of the el package set, so the precondition of this CVE cannot be met. Red Hat's own verdict reads "Not vulnerable. OPIE for PAM is not shipped with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 2.1, 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7"; the enumeration stops at 7 only because the statement was written in 2007 - no opie/pam_opie package exists in any EL-family repository (RHEL, CentOS, AlmaLinux, Rocky, Oracle) or in EPEL for el8+, so the same reasoning carries forward to el8/el9/el10. Red Hat records this verdict ONLY in the free-text `statement` field: there is no `package_state` entry and no OVAL definition in either rhel-N.oval.xml or rhel-N-including-unpatched.oval.xml, so no structured feed can supply it and the auto-sourced backfill leaves it UNCERTAIN. NVD compounds this by carrying the record with no version bounds at all, so it matches every OpenSSH release ever published - the same structural defect already gated for CVE-2008-3844. Verified 2026-09-09.

Ubuntu marks every release it triaged not-affected (trusty to mantic, "see notes"): the researchers used a modified sshd, there is no indication the Ubuntu openssh package can be exploited the same way, and upstream declined the issue as not exploitable in practice. 24.04 was never triaged, so the tracker carries no row for it; 24.04 ships the same openssh code base (9.6p1) and the same reasoning holds. The attack needs a local Rowhammer/DRAM bit-flip primitive (CVSS AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) and cannot be reached by an external scan. Verified 2026-10-22.

OPIE for PAM is not part of the Ubuntu archive, so the precondition of this CVE cannot be met: the libpam-opie and opie source packages were deleted in oneiric (11.10) and exist in no later Ubuntu release (Launchpad publishing history), and Debian, which Ubuntu's openssh is built from, ships no libpam-opie in any suite either. Ubuntu's tracker last triaged this CVE for gutsy (7.10, priority negligible), so it carries no row for a supported release. NVD lists the record with no version bounds, so it matches every OpenSSH release. Verified 2026-10-22.
